nodes.summary: Let $F_m$ denote the $m$-th Fibonacci number, with $F_0 = 0$ and $F_1 = 1$. If $p$ is an odd prime with $p \equiv 2 \pmod 3$ and $p \equiv 2$ or $3 \pmod 5$, and $n = 2p$ or $n = 4p$, then $F_n$ is odd and $F_{F_n + 2}$ leaves remainder $1$ on division by $F_n$.
nodes.title: Odd Fibonacci numbers $F_n$ with $F_{F_n + 2} \equiv 1 \pmod{F_n}$

nodes.summary: Write $F_t$ for the $t$-th Fibonacci number. Let $m > 1$ be a natural number and let $\pi$ be a positive integer with $F_\pi \equiv 0 \pmod{m}$ and $F_{\pi+1} \equiv 1 \pmod{m}$ such that $\pi \le t$ for every positive integer $t$ with $F_t \equiv 0 \pmod{m}$ and $F_{t+1} \equiv 1 \pmod{m}$; that is, $\pi$ is the Pisano period of $m$. Then $\pi = m$ if and only if $m = 24 \cdot 5^{\lambda - 1}$ for some integer…
nodes.title: Fulton–Morris theorem on Pisano periods equal to the modulus

nodes.summary: Let $F_i$ denote the $i$-th Fibonacci number, with $F_1 = F_2 = 1$. There are infinitely many odd positive integers $k$ such that $k$ divides $F_1 + F_2 + \dots + F_k$.
nodes.title: Infinitely many odd $k$ divide the sum of the first $k$ Fibonacci numbers

nodes.summary: Let $F_n$ denote the $n$-th Fibonacci number and $\pi(m)$ the Pisano period of $m$. For every even natural number $n > 1$, $\pi(F_n)$ divides $2n$.
nodes.title: The Pisano period of $F_n$ divides $2n$ for even $n$

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, the Pisano period $\pi(n)$ is the minimal period of the pair $(0, 1)$ under the Fibonacci step $(a, b) \mapsto (b, a + b)$ on $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$: the least $k \ge 1$ such that $k$ applications of the step map $(0, 1)$ back to $(0, 1)$, or $0$ if there is no such $k$ (as for $n = 0$, where $\mathbb{Z}/0\mathbb{Z} = \mathbb{Z}$).
nodes.title: Pisano period

nodes.summary: Let $p > 5$ be a prime, let $F_i$ denote the $i$-th Fibonacci number, with $F_1 = F_2 = 1$, and let $S = F_1 + F_2 + \dots + F_p$. If $p \equiv 1$ or $4 \pmod 5$, then $S$ leaves remainder $1$ on division by $p$; if $p \equiv 2$ or $3 \pmod 5$, then $S$ leaves remainder $p - 2$ on division by $p$; and in every case $p$ does not divide $S$.
nodes.title: Sum of the first $p$ Fibonacci numbers modulo a prime $p$

nodes.summary: Let $\pi(n)$ denote the Pisano period of $n$. As $N \to \infty$, the minimum of the real numbers $\pi(n)/n$ over the integers $1 \le n \le N - 1$ (defined for $N \ge 2$) tends to $0$.
nodes.title: The minimum of $\pi(n)/n$ over $1 \le n < N$ tends to zero

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
